name: Hannah Chappatte

education.notes: Graduated 2019. Founded Hybr while experiencing the student rental market firsthand in her final year.

careerSteps.role: BA Liberal Arts student (and rental-market reluctant operator)
keyDecisions: Chose Liberal Arts (a non-vocational degree) rather than a business or CS path — broadened her lens before going deep.
Got 'fixated' with how broken the student rental experience was in her final year — turned personal pain into product hypothesis.
Stayed in Bristol post-graduation to launch Hybr there before expanding — built where she had the most density of users.
lessons: A non-vocational undergrad (Liberal Arts) is NOT a disqualifier for founding — Hybr's wedge is operational, not technical.
Personal-pain market signal is a faster route to PMF than methodical customer interviews when you're young: your own life is the user research.
Found where you have density (Bristol students) before going broad — the cheapest GTM is your own network.
careerSteps.notes: Per Property Week / Estates Gazette / Bristol University coverage.

keyDecisions: Founded Hybr in 2020 — student-accommodation matching platform connecting students with vetted private landlords, agents and PBSA providers.
Built a marketplace that works for both sides: students get verified listings + referencing, landlords get pre-qualified tenants who pass checks.
Expanded 18-fold in 12 months between 2022 and 2023 — sustained hypergrowth without raising large early rounds.
Raised a £3.24M seed round led by BlackWood Ventures in 2024 — selectively after traction proved itself, not before.
Grew to ~150,000 rooms on the platform across Bristol, Liverpool, London and Manchester by 2025.
lessons: Marketplace business → raise selectively AFTER demonstrating non-linear growth, not before — investors compete to back you, not the other way round.
Geographic-cluster expansion (Bristol → Liverpool → London → Manchester) compounds operating learnings before chasing scale.
Building infrastructure for an industry (private landlords + PBSA + agents) that lacks coordination is a sticky moat — fragmented industries are where marketplaces win.
Found at 22 from a Liberal Arts degree — neither technical-CS nor business-school background is a prerequisite for proptech founding.
careerSteps.notes: Founded 2020 in Bristol. 20 staff by 2025; ~150,000 rooms on the platform. £3.24M seed BlackWood Ventures 2024. 18-fold expansion in 12 months reported (2022-2023).

outcomes.currentStatus: Founder & CEO of Hybr (UK). ~150,000 rooms on the platform; 20 staff; expanded 18-fold in 12 months 2022→2023. £3.24M seed led by BlackWood Ventures (2024).

lessons.lesson: Personal-pain market signal — Chappatte's own awful student rental experience in her final year at Bristol became the founding hypothesis.
A non-vocational undergrad (Liberal Arts) is not a disqualifier for proptech / marketplace founding — operational wedges don't require CS or MBA.
Raise selectively AFTER traction (18x growth, then a £3.24M seed) — marketplace founders should let traction draw investors rather than chasing rounds early.
Geographic-cluster expansion (Bristol → Liverpool → London → Manchester) compounds operating learnings cheaply.
